mainTopic: Healing on שבת, the olive reed, and the gradual permission to move כלים on שבת (מוקצה)
overview: This amud opens at the end of a מחלוקת between רב נחמן and רב ששת about aligning a newborn's limbs on שבת. Each one's proof is pushed away by the other. A new משנה then teaches that an olive-turning reed with a knot can become טמא, because the hollow by the knot is a small receptacle. Either way, the reed may be moved on שבת. Next, רבי יוסי rules that all כלים may be moved on שבת except a large saw and a plow blade, and רב נחמן and אביי add similar guarded tools to that list. A ברייתא shows that this rule started very strict, with only three eating tools allowed, and was relaxed in stages. אביי and רבא disagree about what those stages were, and אביי challenges רבא from the case of a mortar. רבי חנינא says the strict stage dates from the days of נחמיה, when people were careless about שבת. רבי אלעזר then lists early משניות from before כלים were permitted, and the quote about the poles continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ששת rejects the emetic proof
steps.stepSummary: This amud begins with the last words of רב נחמן's proof: one may not drink אפיקטויזין on שבת. רב ששת answers that drinking an emetic is unusual behavior, while handling a baby's limbs is ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One may not drink] an emetic on שבת. And רב ששת answers: there, it is not the normal way of doing things; here, it is the normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The first two words finish רב נחמן's proof that healing actions are forbidden on שבת. Then רב ששת pushes that proof away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן compared aligning a baby's limbs to drinking an emetic, which is forbidden on שבת because it is clearly a medical act. רב ששת says the cases are different. Nobody drinks an emetic except as medicine, so it looks like healing. But people handle and straighten a baby's body all the time, so it does not look like a medical treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: An emetic, a drink taken to make a person vomit
It is not its normal way (unusual behavior)
There / here, the standard way to contrast two cases

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. 'אפיקטויזין בשבת' is the END of רב נחמן's quoted proof (the rule that one does not drink an emetic on שבת). It is not a new statement.

phrases.english: [one may not drink] an emetic on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: This wraps up רב נחמן's proof that started on the previous daf.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet [answers]:
There, it is not the normal way;
here, it is the normal way.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (for the opening tail of רב נחמן's proof)
steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָתָם — לָאו אוֹרְחֵיהּ, הָכָא — אוֹרְחֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's proof, which began on the previous daf
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between drinking an emetic and aligning a baby's limbs
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An emetic is only drunk as medicine, so it is obviously healing. Handling a baby is ordinary daily behavior.

steps.title: רב ששת's proof from removing a thorn
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a source for his lenient view. A משנה allows using a sewing needle on שבת to take out a thorn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: From where do I say this? As we learned in a משנה: a hand needle may be moved to take out a thorn with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת now goes on the offense. He brings a משנה to prove that some body-care actions are allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking out a thorn is a kind of treatment for the body. Yet the משנה permits using a needle for it. So, says רב ששת, not every action that helps the body is forbidden, and aligning a baby's limbs should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (I have a source for my view)
As we learned in a משנה
A hand needle (an ordinary sewing needle)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
From where do I say it?
As we learned in a Mishnah: a hand needle,
[may be moved] to remove a thorn with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending himself, רב ששת brings positive support for his view
steps.raayaObject: That aligning a baby's limbs on שבת is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting the use of a hand needle to remove a thorn on שבת

steps.title: רב נחמן rejects the thorn proof
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that a thorn is only a foreign object stuck in the body. Aligning a baby's limbs changes the body itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן answers: there, the thorn is just deposited in the body; here, it is not something deposited.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes away רב ששת's proof by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling out a thorn removes something foreign. It does not change the body. Aligning limbs reshapes the body itself, which is real healing and resembles finishing the making of an object. So the thorn case proves nothing about the baby, and the מחלוקת stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Deposited, placed in as a foreign object (not part of the body)
Not deposited, part of the body itself

steps.whatToRemember: Each side's proof was pushed away. Emetic ≠ baby, because an emetic is unusual and a baby's handling is normal. Thorn ≠ baby, because a thorn is foreign while the limbs are the body itself.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman [answers]:
There, it is deposited;
here, it is not deposited.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן: הָתָם — פְּקִיד, הָכָא — לָא פְּקִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's proof from step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between removing a thorn and aligning a baby's limbs
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A thorn is a foreign object, so removing it changes nothing in the body. Aligning limbs changes the body itself.

steps.title: משנה: the olive-turning reed
steps.stepSummary: A reed used to turn olives can become טמא if it has a knot at its top, and cannot if it has none. Either way, it may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A reed used for olives: if there is a knot at its top, it can become טמא; if not, it cannot become טמא. Either way, it may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives two separate rules about the reed: one about טומאה and one about moving it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The knot decides whether the reed counts as a כלי that can become טמא. For שבת, however, the knot makes no difference. With or without it, the reed is a usable object that may be moved for a permitted use.

keyTerms.meaning: A reed used to turn over olives

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. The knot matters for טומאה only. Moving the reed on שבת is permitted in both cases.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A reed for olives,
if there is a knot at its top,
it can become impure;
and if not, it cannot become impure.
Either way,
it may be moved on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knotted olive reed can become טמא and an unknotted one cannot. Both may be moved on שבת.

steps.title: Why should a flat stick become impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the reed can become טמא at all. It is a פשוטי כלי עץ (a flat wooden item with no container), and such items need to be like a שק (sack), which holds things.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why? It is a flat wooden item, and flat wooden items do not become טמא. What is the reason? We need it to be similar to a sack.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first rule of the משנה, that a knotted reed can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wooden items become טמא only if they have a receptacle, like the שק mentioned in the תורה. A reed is just a flat stick with nothing to hold anything, so a knot should not make it a כלי. This is the problem the next step must solve.

keyTerms.meaning: Flat wooden items with no receptacle
Similar to a sack (which has a space to hold things)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the basic rule of טומאת כלים for wood: only something with a receptacle, like a שק, can become טמא.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why?
It is a flat wooden item,
and flat wooden items
do not become impure.
What is the reason?
We require [something] similar to a sack.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the טומאה ruling of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a knotted reed can become טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reed is a flat wooden item with no receptacle. Such items must resemble a שק to become טמא, and a plain reed does not.

steps.title: The knot forms a tiny receptacle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the name of רבי נחמיה explains that while turning the olives, the worker flips the reed and looks into the hollow by the knot to check for oil. That hollow counts as a receptacle.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי נחמיה: when one turns the olives, he flips the reed over and looks into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that the knotted reed really does have a small receptacle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beside the knot there is a small cavity that collects oil. The worker checks it to see whether the olives are ready for pressing. Because this cavity holds something and is actually used, the reed is no longer a flat item. It is like a שק, so it can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the name of
He flips it and looks into it

steps.whatToRemember: A knotted olive reed can become טמא because the hollow near the knot is a small receptacle used to check for oil. Without a knot, it is a flat stick and stays טהור. Either way, it may be moved on שבת.

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Nechemya:
At the time that he turns over the olives,
he flips it over and looks into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the object: the reed has a functional receptacle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reed is just a flat stick with no container, so it should never become טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: The cavity by the knot holds oil and is used for checking, so it is a receptacle like a שק

steps.title: רבי יוסי: All tools may be moved except two
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that every tool may be moved on שבת except a large saw and a plow blade.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יוסי says: All tools may be moved on שבת, except for the large saw and the blade of a plow.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי יוסי gives a broad lenient rule that all tools may be moved on שבת, with only two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Owners are very careful with these two tools because they must stay sharp and could easily be damaged. So the owner sets them aside completely in his mind and never uses them for anything else. This puts them in the category of מוקצה מחמת חסרון כיס.

keyTerms.meaning: The blade (or spike) of a plow
An item set aside because the owner fears it will be damaged and cause him a money loss

steps.confusionAlert: These two tools are not forbidden just because they are used for forbidden work. Many work tools may be moved for a permitted use. These two are forbidden because their owners are extra careful with them and never use them for anything else.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Yosei says:
All utensils may be moved,
except for the large saw
and the blade of a plow.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים נִיטָּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that starts a new topic, separate from the reed and olives discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All tools may be moved on שבת except the large saw and the plow blade, because they are set aside out of fear of damage.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The launderer's tool is like a plow blade
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן adds a launderer's tool to רבי יוסי's list of forbidden tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן said: The launderer's sprinkler is like the blade of a plow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. רב נחמן names another tool that gets the same law as the plow blade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה named only two tools, but the reason behind it applies to more. A launderer is very protective of this tool and never uses it for other purposes. So it is also set aside and may not be moved on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A launderer's sprinkler (a tool used to sprinkle water on clothes)
Is similar to / is treated like

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Nachman said:
This sprinkler of launderers
is like the blade of a plow.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי אוּכְלָא דְקַצָּרֵי כְּיָתֵד שֶׁל מַחֲרֵישָׁה דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the משנה's category and adds another item to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A launderer's sprinkler has the same law as a plow blade and may not be moved on שבת.

steps.title: אביי: Three professional knives are like a plow blade
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a shoemaker's knife, a butcher's knife, and a carpenter's drawknife to the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A shoemaker's knife, a butcher's knife, and a carpenter's drawknife are like the blade of a plow.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues the same pattern. He lists three more professional tools that get the plow blade's law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these is a skilled worker's blade that must stay sharp. The craftsman is careful never to use it for anything else. Because of this care, the tool is set aside completely and may not be moved on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב נחמן and אביי show that the משנה's list is only examples. The true rule is: any tool its owner guards from other use because he fears damage.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The knife of shoemakers,
and the knife of a butcher,
and the drawknife of carpenters
are like the blade of a plow.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַרְבָּא דְאוּשְׁכָּפֵי וְסַכִּינָא דְאַשְׁכָּבְתָּא וַחֲצִינָא דְנַגָּרֵי כְּיָתֵד שֶׁל מַחֲרֵישָׁה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel addition to רב נחמן's. It widens the same category with more examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shoemaker's knife, a butcher's knife, and a carpenter's drawknife have the same law as a plow blade.

steps.title: At first, only three eating tools could be moved
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that originally only three tools, all used for eating, could be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: At first they used to say that only three tools may be moved on שבת: a knife for cutting a fig cake, a spoon-fork for cleaning the grime from a pot, and a small table knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells the history behind the משנה's rule. This first part describes the original, very strict starting point, and it sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start, the rule was the reverse of רבי יוסי's. Almost every tool was forbidden, and only three tools needed for eating were allowed. This shows that the broad leniency in the משנה came later.

keyTerms.meaning: A knife for cutting a pressed cake of dried figs
A combined spoon and fork used to clean grime from a pot

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
At first they would say
three utensils may be moved on Shabbat:
a knife for a cake of dried figs,
and a spoon-fork for the filth of a pot,
and a small knife that is on the table.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים שְׁלֹשָׁה כֵּלִים נִיטָּלִין בַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from adding tools to the list to the historical background of the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, only three tools needed for eating could be moved on שבת.

steps.title: The rule was relaxed step by step until the final ruling
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים loosened the rule again and again, until they reached רבי יוסי's ruling: all tools except the large saw and the plow blade.
steps.simpleTranslation: They permitted more, and again permitted more, and again permitted more, until they said: All tools may be moved on שבת, except the large saw and the blade of a plow.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the history. The rule was relaxed in stages until it matched the final ruling of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three rounds of 'they permitted' show a slow, gradual process. The last stage repeats the exact words of רבי יוסי's ruling. This tells us his ruling is the final word and the endpoint of the whole process.

keyTerms.meaning: And they went back (and did it again)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's two forbidden tools (and the others added by רב נחמן and אביי) are forbidden because owners guard them from any other use. The ברייתא shows the rule began very strict and became lenient in stages, ending with רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: The end of the ברייתא repeats the משנה word for word. This is not a new ruling. It shows that the משנה is the final stage of the gradual relaxation.

phrases.english: They permitted, and then they permitted again,
and then they permitted again,
until they said:
All utensils may be moved on Shabbat,
except for the large saw
and the blade of a plow.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתִּירוּ וְחָזְרוּ וְהִתִּירוּ וְחָזְרוּ וְהִתִּירוּ עַד שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's history. It moves from the strict starting point to the final lenient ruling found in the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After gradual stages of relaxation, the final rule is that all tools may be moved on שבת except the large saw and the plow blade, as רבי יוסי taught.

steps.title: What were the stages of permission?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what each stage of 'they permitted, and again they permitted' in the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it mean: they permitted, then they permitted again, then they permitted again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא from the last step. This sets up the next move, where אביי and רבא each explain the stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the rules were loosened several times but did not say what changed each time. The גמרא wants each stage spelled out.

phrases.english: What is 'they permitted, and then they permitted,'
and then they permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the stages in the ברייתא of step 10-11 actually were.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly was permitted at each stage of loosening.

steps.title: אביי's explanation of the stages
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the stages by the reason for moving the tool and by whether it needs one hand or two.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: First they permitted moving a tool meant for permitted work in order to use it. Then they permitted moving such a tool because its space was needed. Then they permitted moving a tool meant for forbidden work in order to use it, but not because its space was needed. Even then, only a tool that could be moved with one hand was allowed, not one that needed two hands. Finally they said: all tools may be moved on שבת, even with two hands.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by listing the stages of loosening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses two dividing lines. The first is the reason for moving the tool: to use it (לצורך גופו) or to free up its spot (לצורך מקומו). The second is the type of tool: one meant for permitted work or one meant for forbidden work. Even after these stages, a limit remained (וַעֲדַיִין) that only a tool movable with one hand was allowed. The final stage removed that limit and allowed even two hands.

keyTerms.meaning: A tool whose normal use is permitted on שבת
A tool whose normal use is forbidden on שבת
In order to use the tool itself
Because you need the spot where the tool is

steps.confusionAlert: 'לצורך גופו' does not mean 'for the person's body.' It means using the tool itself for a permitted job, like cracking nuts with a hammer.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They permitted an object whose function is permitted
for the purpose of using it itself,
and then they permitted an object whose function is permitted
for the purpose of its place,
and then they permitted an object whose function is prohibited:
for the purpose of using it itself, yes;
for the purpose of its place, no.
And still, with one hand, yes;
with his two hands, no,
until they said:
All tools may be moved on Shabbat,
and even with two hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Stages: permitted-use tool for itself, then for its place, then forbidden-use tool for itself only, then even tools needing two hands.

steps.title: רבא objects to אביי's distinction
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the ברייתא says simply 'they permitted,' so there is no reason to split using a tool from needing its space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: The ברייתא just says 'they permitted.' What difference does it make whether it is to use the tool or because its space is needed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once moving is allowed at all, the ברייתא gives no hint of a difference between using the tool and needing its space. So אביי's stages rest on a distinction the source does not support.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
After all, it teaches 'they permitted';
what difference to me whether for itself,
what difference to me whether for its place?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: מִכְּדֵי הִתִּירוּ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's split between לצורך גופו and לצורך מקומו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's plain wording 'הִתִּירוּ' does not support splitting the two purposes.

steps.title: רבא's own explanation of the stages
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the stages differently: use and space together, then protecting from the sun, then forbidden-use tools, then tools needing two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: First they permitted moving a tool meant for permitted work, whether to use it or because its space was needed. Then they permitted moving it from the sun to the shade. Then they permitted moving a tool meant for forbidden work to use it or because its space was needed, but not from the sun to the shade. Even then, only a tool one person could carry was allowed, not one that needed two people. Finally they said: all tools may be moved on שבת, even by two people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the question of step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, using a tool and needing its space are one stage. The new line he draws is moving a tool just to protect it (מחמה לצל). That is allowed for permitted-use tools but not for forbidden-use tools. His last limit is about how many people are needed to carry it, not how many hands.

keyTerms.meaning: From the sun to the shade: moving a tool just to protect it

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: stages are use, then space, then forbidden tools for use only, then two hands. רבא: stages are use or space, then from sun to shade, then forbidden tools for use or space (not sun to shade), then two people.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
They permitted an object whose function is permitted

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְצוֹרֶךְ גּוּפוֹ וּבֵין לְצוֹרֶךְ מְקוֹמוֹ,
phrases.english: whether for using it itself or for its place,
and then they permitted from the sun to the shade.
And then they permitted an object whose function is prohibited:
for using it itself and for its place, yes;
from the sun to the shade, no.
And still, by one person, yes;
by two people, no,
until they said:
All tools may be moved on Shabbat,
even by two people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's explanation after the objection of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Stages: permitted-use tool for itself or its place, then from sun to shade, then forbidden-use tool for itself or its place (not sun to shade), then even tools needing two people.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the mortar
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a teaching that a mortar may be moved only if it has garlic in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: A mortar: if there is garlic in it, you may move it. If not, you may not move it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation with an earlier teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mortar is a tool meant for forbidden work (grinding). רבא says such a tool may be moved to use it or for its space. So why does this teaching forbid moving an empty mortar?

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from an earlier source)

phrases.english: Abaye challenged him:
A mortar: if there is garlic in it,
one may move it;
and if not, one may not move it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's explanation in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a forbidden-use tool may be moved for its use or its space
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An empty mortar is forbidden to move, which seems to contradict רבא's broad permission.

steps.title: The mortar case means sun to shade
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the mortar teaching is about moving it just to protect it from the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? Moving it from the sun to the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his explanation by narrowing the case of the mortar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא, a forbidden-use tool still may not be moved only to protect it. If the empty mortar is being moved just to get it out of the sun, the ban fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
From the sun to the shade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching forbids moving an empty mortar for any reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: It forbids moving it only to protect it (מחמה לצל), just as רבא said.

steps.title: Second challenge: the item used to cut meat
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a teaching that, once meat was cut on the item, everyone agrees it may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him again: Both sides agree that if one cut meat on it, it is forbidden to move it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second challenge to רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching comes from a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about יום טוב. Both agree that once the meat has been cut on the item, it may not be moved, because it is no longer needed for the festival and is again just a tool meant for forbidden work. רבא would allow moving such a tool for its use or its space, yet this teaching seems to forbid moving it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (both sides of a dispute)

phrases.english: He challenged him:
And they agree that if he cut meat on it,
that it is forbidden to move it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאִם קִצֵּב עָלָיו בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבא, parallel to step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's broad permission for forbidden-use tools
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blanket ban on moving the item seems to contradict רבא.

steps.title: This case also means sun to shade
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the same answer: the ban is only on moving it to protect it from the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means from the sun to the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the second challenge the same way as the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban applies only when the item is moved just to protect it, which רבא still forbids for forbidden-use tools. So both challenges fit his view.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רבא, a tool meant for forbidden work may be moved to use it or to free its space, but not just to protect it (מחמה לצל). That limit answers both of אביי's challenges.

phrases.english: Here too, from the sun to the shade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 using the same answer as step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The item may not be moved for any reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: It may not be moved only to protect it (מחמה לצל).

steps.title: The strict משנה was taught in the days of נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that the משנה limiting which כלים may be moved was taught in the time of נחמיה, when people were treating שבת lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: This משנה was taught in the days of נחמיה בן חכליה, as it is written: 'In those days I saw in Judea people treading winepresses on שבת and bringing in heaps.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא tells us when the strict משנה about moving only a few כלים on שבת was taught: in the days of נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse shows that people in נחמיה's time were openly doing מלאכה on שבת. Because of this, the חכמים made the rules extra strict to teach people to respect שבת. This explains why the early rule was so limited before it was later relaxed.

keyTerms.meaning: Nechemiah son of Chachalyah, a leader in the early Second Temple period

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the historical reason behind the strict stage: it was a temporary גזירה to fix carelessness, which is why it could later be relaxed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
In the days of Nechemiah son of Chachalyah
this mishnah was taught,
as it is written:
"In those days I saw in Judea
people treading winepresses on Shabbat
and bringing in heaps."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: בִּימֵי נְחֶמְיָה בֶּן חֲכַלְיָה נִשְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the אביי–רבא debate on the stages of permission, the גמרא steps back to explain when the earliest strict stage was taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strict משנה on moving כלים was taught in נחמיה's era, as a response to widespread שבת violation.

steps.title: Four topics taught before utensils were permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר lists four topics whose משניות were all taught before the permission to move כלים on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Rods, poles, the גלוסטרא, and a mortar — all of these were taught before the permission of utensils.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר names four topics and says their strict משניות come from the early period, before moving כלים was allowed. The גמרא will now show the source for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some משניות seem to forbid moving items that today we would allow. רבי אלעזר explains they are not the final law; they were taught during the early strict period. This setup prepares the next steps, which bring each source.

keyTerms.meaning: rods (golden rods between the loaves of the לחם הפנים)
poles (used in the בית המקדש to hang the קרבן פסח)
the thick knobbed end of a door bolt
the permission to move utensils on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying these items are always forbidden. He is saying the strict משניות about them reflect an early stage that was later relaxed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Rods, and poles,
the gelostera, and a mortar —
all of them were taught before the permission of utensils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the historical theme of רבי חנינא by identifying specific משניות from the early strict period.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משניות about קנים, מקלות, גלוסטרא, and מדוכה reflect the time before moving כלים was permitted.

steps.title: The source for the rods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה that moving the rods of the לחם הפנים does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rods — as we learned: Neither arranging the rods nor removing them overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the first source on רבי אלעזר's list: the משנה about the rods of the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says one may not set up or take out the rods on שבת, meaning they were treated as forbidden to move. According to רבי אלעזר, this strictness is from before כלים were permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rods — as we learned:
Neither arranging the rods
nor removing them
overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the first item in רבי אלעזר's list.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה about the rods reflects the early strict stage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מנחות: neither arranging nor removing the rods overrides שבת.

steps.title: The source for the poles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source about the smooth poles used to hang and skin the קרבן פסח, and that they were not used when ערב פסח fell on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Poles — as we learned: There were thin, smooth poles there, and one places it on his shoulder and on the shoulder of his friend, and hangs and flays. רבי אלעזר said: When the fourteenth fell on שבת, one places... (continues)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the second source: the poles in the בית המקדש used to hang the קרבן פסח for skinning. It begins quoting that on שבת they were not used, and this passage stops mid-sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two people held a pole on their shoulders and hung the animal on it to skin it. When the fourteenth of ניסן fell on שבת, they used another method instead of the poles, showing the poles were treated as forbidden to move. רבי אלעזר says this reflects the time before כלים were permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase ends at מַנִּיחַ — the sentence continues on the next amud, describing the alternative method used on שבת.

phrases.english: Poles — as we learned:
There were thin, smooth poles there,
and one places it on his shoulder
and on the shoulder of his friend,
and hangs (the animal) and flays it.
Rabbi Elazar said:
When the fourteenth (of Nisan) fell on Shabbat,
one places
phrases.notes: Sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the second item in רבי אלעזר's list.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה about the poles (not used on שבת) reflects the early strict stage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פסחים about the smooth poles used for hanging and skinning the קרבן פסח.
